$schema-note: Every difference between a v9 frame and the implementation lands in exactly one class. Gate B reads this file and enforces the rules below — the classification is not advisory prose.

classes.MUST-FIX: Clearly violates v9 with no functionality or accessibility reason. Implement the v9 design exactly. BLOCKS its frame until closed. No approval needed to fix — fixing toward v9 is the mandate.
classes.APPROVED-DEVIATION: Existing functionality or accessibility requires something different from v9. DO NOT MODIFY until the owner explicitly approves. Blocks its frame while status is pending.
classes.PRODUCT-DECISION: The v9 HTML specifies a different workflow or different copy, and choosing between them is the owner's call, not an engineering one. DO NOT MODIFY until the owner explicitly approves. Blocks its frame while status is pending.
classes.NOT-BUILT: The surface or its server support does not exist yet. Leave untouched until its assigned migration task runs. Does not block a frame for a defect it cannot have.

deviations.summary: Free-form voice intent routing has no surface in the app since ruling #30 removed VoiceCommandHero

The orb is a voice affordance in NAME (mic icon, hold menu) but not in behaviour: nav-dock.tsx:59 is `onTap={() => router.push(action.href)}` and voice-menu.tsx:87 is `router.push(row.href)`. Ruling #30's stated rationale was 'the dock orb remains the single global voice affordance'. That premise is true of the icon and false of the behaviour, so the ruling was likely made without this being visible.

deviations.summary: A rejected consultation made its visit permanently un-recordable — the root cause of #44
deviations.reason: POST /consultations returns the EXISTING consultation for a visit whatever its status (consultations.ts findUnique on visitId). Once a doctor taps Re-record — which posts /consultations/:id/reject and sets status REJECTED — and then leaves the screen or the app reloads, tapping Record for that patient in the queue re-enters the same REJECTED consultation. deriveStateFromView returns {kind:'REJECTED'} and the consult page router.replace's back to /consult. The doctor taps Record, is bounced to the queue, and the visit can never be recorded again — silently, with no error. Reproduced against the live stack: D2/D3/D4/D5 capture now dead-ends on the queue screen.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED AS MUST-FIX (owner, verbatim): "A REJECTED consultation represents a rejected recording/processing attempt, NOT a permanently unusable visit. POST /consultations for a visit that already has a REJECTED consultation must reuse that existing consultation and reset it to PENDING_REVIEW so the doctor can record again... The rejection itself MUST remain durable in AuditLog via CONSULTATION_REJECTED. Do NOT drop the unique Consultation.visitId constraint. Do NOT create a second consultation record for the same visit as part of this fix. Do NOT remove or weaken the audit trail."
deviations.fixedIn: apps/api/src/routes/consultations.ts — POST /consultations resets a REJECTED consultation in place: status PENDING_REVIEW, and every field that is the rejected ATTEMPT's own output cleared (structuredData, rejectedById, rejectedReason, rawTranscriptEnc, audioUrl, audioStorageKey, audioDurationMs, languageCode, provider, sttLatencyMs, extractionLatencyMs, safetyWarnings). The schema was inspected per the ruling: those are precisely the transient/derived columns of one recording. Patient, Visit, ConsultationEdit and AuditLog are untouched, the unique visitId constraint stands, and no second row is created. A CONSULTATION_REOPENED audit row records the reset. Regression: apps/api/test/consultation-reject-then-rerecord.test.ts covers all eight required proofs. Clearing the transcript and audio key is the safety half — without it the next take would inherit the abandoned recording's dictation.

deviations.summary: Frame 27's "Swap → Azithro 500" — no drug-substitution knowledge base exists
deviations.reason: The frame resolves an allergy conflict by swapping to a NAMED alternative antibiotic, and frame 28 shows the result ('swapped for Amoxicillin · allergy-safe'). Nothing in the app knows that azithromycin is the penicillin-safe substitute: SafetyWarning carries code, message, field and detail — no alternative — and there is no substitution table anywhere in the API. Hardcoding one inside a UI task would be inventing prescribing advice, which is the single thing this product must never do. The conflict rail ships with the frame's full anatomy (red rail, red drug name, one factual line, inline action) and the action is 'Remove', which is the resolution the safety model actually recognises (isResolved: the flagged medicine is no longer prescribed). It says Remove rather than Swap so the doctor is never told the app chose a replacement drug.
deviations.openQuestion: Build drug substitution? It needs a clinical data source, an owner for its correctness, and a decision about liability — the app would be suggesting a specific prescription. Recommend a dedicated task with clinical sign-off, not a migration task.
deviations.reclassified: 2026-09-07 - was NOT-BUILT/open, which read as work still to come. It is not: product rule 6 ('AI must not invent medication substitutions') forbids the swap permanently, and no drug-substitution knowledge base is planned. The card resolves a conflict by REMOVING the drug -- the resolution the safety model actually recognises -- and the button says 'Remove' rather than implying the app chose a replacement. Reclassified so the ledger states a settled decision instead of a pending task.

deviations.summary: The FINDINGS and PROCEDURE prose sections have no extraction fields behind them

deviations.summary: Confirm stays available over an allergy conflict; the dentist decides and the override is audited
deviations.reason: Frame 27 shows 'Confirm & save' disabled while the allergy conflict is unresolved, and the task brief repeats it. That is a CLINICAL POLICY change, not a visual one. Today allergy_conflict is an advisory warning, not a blocking error: the API's own prompt says 'Do NOT remove the prescription — flag it; the doctor decides', and confirming over a live warning is a supported, audited path (confirmedWithWarning -> CONSULTATION_CONFIRMED_WITH_WARNING). Disabling Confirm would remove a doctor's documented authority to prescribe against a flag they have judged — for example a recorded 'rash' that they know to be tolerable. Implemented as today: Confirm is gated by BLOCKING errors only, and the conflict is drawn loudly on the drug.
deviations.openQuestion: Should an unresolved allergy conflict HARD-BLOCK confirm, overriding the doctor? Recommend no — keep the override with its audit trail, since the alternative is a clinician unable to file a record they believe is correct. If yes, the API's warning/blocking classification must change too, so the two layers do not disagree.
deviations.ruling: OWNER RULING: 'KEEP Confirm & Save available during an allergy conflict. Do NOT hard-block confirmation. The current behavior is: OdoVox detects/receives an allergy conflict; OdoVox clearly warns the dentist; dentist reviews the conflict; dentist may remove/change the prescription; dentist may explicitly override the warning if clinically appropriate; the override is recorded in the audit trail. Do NOT invent automatic drug substitutions. Do NOT allow Gemini/LLM output to determine whether an allergy conflict is an absolute contraindication. Any future hard-block policy must come from an explicit clinical safety policy/knowledge layer, not visual matching of the V9 frame.'
deviations.fixedIn: No code change — the ruling confirms the behaviour already shipped, and records WHY it is correct rather than incidental. Confirm is gated by BLOCKING errors only; an allergy conflict is advisory, drawn loudly on the drug itself (red rail, red name, one factual line). Overriding it commits through the existing confirmedWithWarning path and lands in AuditLog as CONSULTATION_CONFIRMED_WITH_WARNING. Frame 27's greyed-out CTA is therefore an APPROVED DEVIATION: matching it would remove a clinician's documented authority on the strength of a visual, which the ruling forbids. Related: #51 stays NOT-BUILT — no automatic substitution is invented, and the conflict action removes the drug rather than choosing a replacement.

deviations.summary: Reception's patient rows carried a medical flag; ruled out — reception queue is not a clinical record
deviations.reason:
Reopened at the owner's instruction. I had closed this as an APPROVED-DEVIATION on my own judgement, which was not mine to make.

WHAT THE V9 FRAME SHOWS (frames 32/33): each row is avatar, name, then a glyph strip of TOOTH NUMBER, SITTING PROGRESS DOTS (filled/current/remaining) and DUES in crit — plus a trailing status dot. It reads as a treatment-progress list.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION SHOWS: avatar, name, then AGE, CHIEF COMPLAINT, the first MEDICAL FLAG in crit (DIABETES, HYPERTENSION) and DUES in crit — plus the trailing status dot. It reads as a patient-identity list. The avatar ring and dot now carry live queue state (#62).

LOST BY MATCHING THE FRAME: the medical flag, which is the only place a receptionist opening a record sees a condition before they act, and the frame has nowhere to put it. Age also goes — the everyday disambiguator between two patients with the same name.

GAINED BY MATCHING THE FRAME: which tooth is being treated and how far through the plan the patient is, without opening the record. For a clinic scanning for 'who is mid-RCT' that is the more useful list.

WHICH KIND OF DECISION: primarily WORKFLOW — who is scanning this list and what for. It has a CLINICAL edge, because dropping the medical flag removes safety information from a receptionist-visible surface. It is not a visual decision; both versions are the same component with different facts in it. It also carries a technical cost: tooth + sitting dots require joining every row to its active plan, the widening deferred in #48.
deviations.ruling: OWNER RULING: 'I am choosing the receptionist/queue workflow over exposing clinical information on the queue card. The receptionist-facing patient/queue card should NOT display medical flags or allergies. #69 established the clinical/privacy boundary. Medical flags are clinically relevant to the dentist, not a general receptionist queue surface. The doctor-facing /consult surface already exposes the relevant allergy information. Do not expose medical conditions simply because they happen to exist in the payload. KEEP: patient identity, operational queue information, dues/billing information, complaint if it is already part of the approved workflow. PREFER tooth / treatment sitting / treatment progress IF the required structured data already exists or is introduced by an already-planned task. DO NOT create speculative clinical data. RECEPTION QUEUE ≠ CLINICAL RECORD.'
deviations.openQuestion: Which list is this? Options: (a) keep as-is — identity + safety, no extra query; (b) match the frame — treatment progress, losing the medical flag and needing the plan join; (c) both, dropping age to make room, still needing the join. I recommend (c) if the join is acceptable, since it keeps the safety flag and gains the clinical progress, but this is your ruling and I am not resolving it.
deviations.fixedIn: The medical-flag chip is removed from the /patients row. What remains is what reception works with: identity (name, age), the live queue state on the avatar ring and trailing dot, the complaint, and dues in crit. The doctor still sees allergies where they act on them — prominently on the in-chair card behind DOCTOR/ADMIN (#69). The privacy regression test now treats /patients as a reception surface, so a future edit cannot quietly put flags back.

deviations.summary: The day river counted cancelled appointments and put the chair marker on the wrong patient
deviations.reason: Frame 13's river is the habit hook — one segment per appointment, lime done, dark in the chair. It was fed `appointments.length` raw, so cancellations and no-shows drew as work still ahead: a doctor with three call-offs saw a day that was fuller than it was. And the chair marker was placed at index `done`, assuming the patient in the chair is always the next one after the finished ones — a walk-in seen between booked slots put the dark segment on somebody else. The caption also mixed sources, taking 'to go' from the live queue rather than the day, and omitted the frame's takings clause entirely.
deviations.fixedIn: apps/web/lib/queue/day-river-view.ts — dayShape() filters CANCELLED/NO_SHOW and locates the chair by patientId against the FILTERED list; dayCaption() builds the frame's line and drops clauses that would read as bad news rather than no news ('0 seen · 0 to go · ₹0 in' at 9am describes a disaster; it is just early). 11 tests.

The day river therefore rendered null (it returns null at zero segments), 'Up next' was always empty and the Schedule screen had nothing in it — in every demo and every screenshot, regardless of what else was going on. deviations.summary: The captured river is shorter than frame 13's, because the harness pins the clock to a past date
deviations.reason: The screenshot harness pins the browser clock to 2026-07-13T09:41 so every capture is deterministic — that is where both panels' 'MON · 13 JUL 9:41' comes from. The SERVER runs on real time, so appointments seeded onto that date are weeks overdue as far as the API is concerned and the NO_SHOW sweep correctly retires the future ones. The capture therefore shows the two completed plus the patient in the chair, and the caption's 'to go' and '₹ in' clauses have nothing to say. That is the app behaving correctly on a past-dated fixture, not a defect: on the real today the seeded day renders in full (verified — 2 COMPLETED, 1 CHECKED_IN, 3 SCHEDULED survive).
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved. Closing it properly means either moving the pinned date forward on every capture run or freezing server time too; both are harness changes with their own risks, and neither belongs in a frame task.

deviations.reason: Frame 41 pairs 'Collect ₹3,000' with a 'Remind' action. deviations.summary: The billing headline drops gross 'Billed' for the frame's OUTSTANDING / PAID pair

deviations.summary: The full identity block stays on every tab; v9 shows a compact header on 38/40/41
deviations.reason:
Frame 37 gives the patient a large centred identity block. Frames 38, 40 and 41 replace it with a compact strip — small avatar, name, one action — to buy vertical space for the tab's own content. The implementation keeps the full block throughout.

It is a real difference and it costs roughly 150px on three tabs. It is recorded rather than built because the compact header carries a DIFFERENT action per tab (+ Plan on Cases, PDF on Billing, nothing on Teeth), which is four header variants and a per-tab action contract — more than a restyle, and it interacts with the Task 23 case-detail screen that owns some of those actions. Nothing is lost meanwhile: the identity, the flags and the three stats stay visible on every tab, which is more context than the frames give, not less.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved as layout: no information or action is removed, only repeated.

deviations.summary: Frame 38's "Schedule remaining" — the capability EXISTS; the Cases card does not reach it
deviations.reason:
CORRECTION. This was recorded as NOT-BUILT on the claim that nothing books a plan's outstanding sittings in one action. That claim was wrong, and I did not check hard enough before writing it: POST /appointments/recurring exists, useCreateRecurring() calls it, and the case-detail page already renders a full 'Schedule remaining sittings' control — interval choice (weekly / fortnightly / monthly), a dated preview of every sitting it will create, and a SERIES_UNSCHEDULED error path for slots it cannot place.

So the real gap is navigational, not functional: frame 38's card has no route to a control that is one screen away. Task 23 builds that case-detail screen to the frame and performs its link audit, which is the right place to close this.
deviations.fixedIn: Link audit (Global Constraint 10): every site rendering a plan or procedure name now navigates to case detail — the Overview active-case card, the Teeth tab's tooth panel, the Cases tab's past and secondary plans, the journey's 'Open case', and the PRIMARY active plan's heading, which was the one that did not and is why the control looked missing. 'Schedule remaining sittings' lives on that screen with its interval choice and dated preview; the heading is how frame 38 reaches it. Titles use caseTitle() so the words match the screen they open.

deviations.summary: Journey steps are titled by procedure; v9 titles them by clinical step name
deviations.reason: Frame 38 reads 'Sitting 1 · Access opening', 'Sitting 2 · Cleaning & shaping' — the clinical step each sitting performs. A Sitting has a number and encrypted notes; it has no step-name field, and inventing one per sitting number would be the app asserting a clinical protocol it has no source for (RCT step 2 is not universally 'cleaning & shaping'). Steps are titled by the procedure instead, and the doctor's own note carries the detail where it exists — '28 Jun · extirpation, dressing', which is the same information from an authoritative source.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved: naming clinical steps from a number would be inventing clinical truth.

deviations.summary: Sitting rows show no per-sitting fee — Sitting has no cost field
deviations.reason: Frame 39's sitting rows read '28 Jun · ₹2,500' — what that individual visit cost. A Sitting carries a number, a visit link, encrypted notes and a completion time; it has no money on it, and bills attach to visits and procedures rather than to sittings. Splitting a procedure's bill evenly across its sittings would invent a per-visit price nobody charged. The row shows its date; the money lives on the FEES tile as a plan total, which IS derived from real bill items.
deviations.openQuestion: Should a sitting carry its own charge? It would need a product decision about whether clinics price per sitting or per procedure — they do both — before any schema change.

deviations.summary: The case screen was titled "Treatment Plan" rather than naming the case
deviations.reason: Every other surface refers to this case as 'RCT · Tooth 36'. Landing on a screen headed 'Treatment Plan' makes a doctor check they opened the right one. The header now carries the case's own name, with the sitting chip beside it.

deviations.summary: FEES and NEXT read empty in the capture because the fixture has no billed or booked work
deviations.reason: FEES shows ₹0 / 9,000 because no bill item in the seed points at this plan's procedure — the derivation is correct and tested (7 tests), there is simply nothing paid to report. NEXT reads 'Not booked' for the pinned-clock reason already recorded as #66: the harness freezes the browser at 2026-07-13 while the server runs on real time, so an appointment seeded onto that date is in the past as far as the API is concerned. Both are fixture conditions, not defects.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved as a test-fixture matter, consistent with #66.

deviations.summary: History is a route reached from the overflow menu, not a sixth tab
deviations.reason: The plan allows either, provided no existing tab is removed, and none is. Five tabs already crowd a 370px row — the labels had to lose their padding when 'Overview' truncated — so a sixth would truncate them again. History lives at /patients/[id]/history, reached from the record's overflow menu.
